title: Re-land the validated 64x64 grid-classification head with a convergence-scale training budget (x12 epochs, cosine LR, fresh per-epoch rotations)
hypothesis: Experiment 2's grid-classification architecture was validated, not refuted: on the frames it answered, median error was 743 m vs the kept baseline's 2674.93 m (3.6x better), and it passed both deployment gates (2.5 MiB, 0.63 ms). It failed only the frozen coverage gate (10.75% < 20%). That coverage failure is a symptom of undertraining, not a broken confidence design: its confidence IS posterior mass in a 5x5-cell neighborhood, and after only 8 epochs (33 s wall) the train loss sat at 6.87 nats against a ~3.1-nat soft-label entropy floor - i.e. the posterior was ~3.8 nats (~45x in probability-mass terms) more diffuse than a converged one, so almost no eval frame could concentrate 0.3 mass anywhere. The 8-epoch budget was sized for the harness-proving baseline (loop.sh EPOCHS=8), and loop.sh's own comments document the accepted pattern of train.py applying an internal epoch multiplier. Additionally, the baseline trainer freezes ONE random rotation per crop for the whole run, which at 96 epochs would mean memorizing 6000 fixed images; eval crops carry random headings, so fresh per-epoch rotations are required for the longer budget to convert into generalization (eval blocks are never seen in training - the split is genuinely held-out territory). Prediction: a converged posterior is simultaneously sharper (higher coverage) and more accurate (lower median), fixing the gate failure and the metric with one cause.
method: Two files, one focused change: restore experiment 2's model.py exactly as pre-registered there (64x64 grid logits head, Gaussian-soft-label cross-entropy + soft-argmax aux loss, in-graph soft-argmax coordinate readout, confidence = max 5x5-neighborhood posterior mass - all byte-equivalent to exp 2's brief, deliberately including the unchanged confidence definition as the experimental control), and scale training in train.py: internal EPOCH_MULT=12 (harness's --epochs 8 -> 96 effective epochs), CosineAnnealingLR from 1e-3 to 1e-5 over the full run, and re-extraction of all training crops with fresh random rotation angles at the start of every epoch instead of one frozen rotation at load time. Trunk, data selection, batch size, optimizer family, CLI, and ONNX contract untouched.
expected_outcome: Coverage rises well clear of the 0.2 gate (predict 0.4-0.8) as train CE drops from 6.87 toward the 3.5-4.5 range, and worst-case median error (= the single Berlin/asis cell on this branch) lands in 250-600 m vs the current best 2674.93 m - a 4-10x improvement. Secondary readout: if coverage AGAIN lands under 0.2 despite train CE < 4.5, the 5x5-neighborhood-mass confidence definition is cleanly indicted and the next experiment should redesign the confidence readout, not the training. Gates: identical ONNX to exp 2 (~2.5 MiB, ~0.6 ms host proxy), both comfortably inside budget. Wall-time ~15-25 min on local MPS (96 epochs x ~4 s train + ~5 s/epoch crop re-extraction).
eli5: The last experiment changed the model's job from 'blurt out GPS numbers' to 'point at the right square on a 64x64 checkerboard of Berlin' - and it genuinely got 3.6x more accurate. But it was disqualified by a fairness rule: it was only sure enough to give an answer on 1 in 10 photos, and the rules demand an answer on at least 1 in 5. The catch: it had only been allowed to study for 33 seconds. This experiment brings the same model back and lets it actually study - about 100 passes through the material instead of 8, with every aerial photo shown at a fresh random rotation each pass so it learns places rather than memorizing exact pictures. A model that has properly studied is both more accurate and more confident, which should clear the 'too unsure to answer' disqualification.

stages.name: Camera frame
stages.detail: 128x128 px daytime crop, Berlin only, no synthetic lighting variants

stages.name: Feature extractor
stages.detail: Small 4-layer CNN that shrinks the image step by step into a 128-number summary of what the ground below looks like

stages.name: Map-grid classifier
stages.detail: Scores all 4096 squares of a 64x64 checkerboard laid over Berlin: 'how much does this frame look like each square?'

stages.name: Coordinate + confidence readout
stages.detail: Averages the highest-scoring squares into one precise (lat, lon) point; confidence = how much belief lands in one small neighborhood of the map

stages.name: Training signal
stages.detail: Multiple-choice loss as before, but now studied to convergence: 96 passes instead of 8, a learning rate that eases off as it learns, and every photo re-shown at a fresh random rotation each pass

implementation_brief:
Files: model/model.py and model/train.py. Nothing else. Preserve both fixed contracts exactly: (1) train.py CLI stays `python -m model.train --area A --out-dir D [--data-dir P] [--epochs N] [--max-crops-per-bucket K] [--seed S]` - the harness passes --epochs 8 and --max-crops-per-bucket 6000 and must keep working unchanged; (2) the exported ONNX at <out-dir>/models/<area>.onnx takes one 1x3x128x128 float32 input in [0,1] and returns [[u, v, conf]] with u,v normalized in [0,1] and conf in [0,1] - pipeline/score.py (frozen) depends on this. train_info.json append behavior and the "init": "from-scratch" field stay.

PART A - model/model.py: apply experiment 2's pre-registered design verbatim (it was reverted, so the file is back at the baseline direct-regression state; re-apply in full):
1. Add module-level constants: GRID = 64, LABEL_SIGMA = 1.0 (cells), CONF_POOL = 5.
2. TinyLocNet.__init__: keep the existing conv trunk (chans [3,16,32,64,128], stride-2 3x3 convs + BatchNorm + ReLU) and GAP unchanged. Replace `self.head = nn.Linear(chans[-1], 3)` with `self.head = nn.Linear(chans[-1], GRID * GRID)`. Register two non-trainable buffers of shape (GRID*GRID,): `cell_u` and `cell_v`, normalized cell-center coordinates: for cell index k with row r = k // GRID and col c = k % GRID, cell_u[k] = (c + 0.5) / GRID, cell_v[k] = (r + 0.5) / GRID. (u = horizontal/x = cx/width; v = vertical/y = cy/height. Row-major reshape to (GRID, GRID) puts v on dim 0 and u on dim 1 - keep this layout consistent between buffers, the pooling in forward(), and loss_fn's label construction.)
3. Add method `forward_logits(self, x)`: trunk -> GAP -> head -> (B, GRID*GRID) raw logits. forward() must call forward_logits() so the two graphs cannot diverge.
4. forward(self, x): logits = self.forward_logits(x); p = softmax(logits, dim=1); u = (p * cell_u).sum(1, keepdim=True); v = (p * cell_v).sum(1, keepdim=True) [soft-argmax]; pm = p.reshape(-1, 1, GRID, GRID); neigh = F.avg_pool2d(pm, CONF_POOL, stride=1, padding=CONF_POOL // 2) * (CONF_POOL ** 2); conf = neigh.amax(dim=(1, 2, 3)).unsqueeze(1).clamp(0.0, 1.0); return torch.cat([u, v, conf], dim=1) -> (B, 3). All ops are opset-17-exportable with dynamo=False; keep export_onnx exactly as is. Do NOT alter CONF_POOL or the confidence formula - the unchanged confidence readout is this experiment's control variable.
5. Replace loss_fn entirely, new signature loss_fn(logits, target_uv), logits (B, GRID*GRID) from forward_logits, target_uv (B, 2) in [0,1]:
   - Target cell (float, cell units): gu = target_uv[:, 0] * GRID - 0.5, gv = target_uv[:, 1] * GRID - 0.5.
   - Soft label, vectorized, built under torch.no_grad(): with col grid c (GRID,) and row grid r (GRID,), d2 = (c - gu[:, None, None])**2 + (r[:, None] - gv[:, None, None])**2 broadcast to (B, GRID, GRID) with v/rows on dim 1 and u/cols on dim 2 (same layout as forward()'s reshape); q = softmax(-d2.flatten(1) / (2 * LABEL_SIGMA**2), dim=1) -> (B, GRID*GRID).
   - ce = -(q * log_softmax(logits, dim=1)).sum(1).mean().
   - Aux: p = softmax(logits, 1); uv_hat = stack of (p*cell_u_local).sum(1) and (p*cell_v_local).sum(1); aux = ((uv_hat - target_uv)**2).sum(1).mean(). loss_fn has no module handle - build cell_u_local/cell_v_local from the same formula with torch.arange, cached at module level, moved to logits.device.
   - return ce + 10.0 * aux.
6. Delete the old BCE confidence machinery (the `good` target and binary_cross_entropy). estimate_position and export_onnx stay byte-identical.
Size sanity: ~630k params -> ~2.5 MiB fp32 ONNX (exp 2 measured 2539641 bytes), under the 4 MiB gate. If export lands over 4 MiB, something is wrong - investigate, do not add layers.

PART B - model/train.py (this experiment's actual change):
7. Add module-level constant EPOCH_MULT = 12 with a comment noting the harness passes --epochs 8, giving 96 effective epochs (loop.sh documents this internal-multiplier pattern). In train_area(): total_epochs = epochs * EPOCH_MULT; the epoch loop runs range(total_epochs); progress prints show epoch i+1/total_epochs. In the returned info dict set "epochs": total_epochs and add "harness_epochs": epochs and "epoch_mult": EPOCH_MULT.
8. LR schedule: after creating the Adam optimizer (lr=1e-3 unchanged), create torch.optim.lr_scheduler.CosineAnnealingLR(opt, T_max=total_epochs, eta_min=1e-5) and call scheduler.step() once per epoch after the batch loop.
9. Fresh rotations each epoch: restructure data loading so crop SELECTION happens once but crop EXTRACTION happens per epoch. Replace load_training_tensors with a loader that (a) opens each LIGHTING_BUCKETS image once as a uint8 numpy array and keeps it (iterate LIGHTING_BUCKETS generically - one bucket on this branch, but do not hardcode that), (b) picks min(max_crops_per_bucket, len(crops)) crop records per bucket once with the existing rng.choice(replace=False), (c) builds the fixed target tensor y once via crop_center_norm (targets are rotation-invariant since extract_crop rotates about the crop center). Then at the START of every epoch, build that epoch's x tensor by calling extract_crop(img, c["cx"], c["cy"], angle) with a FRESH angle = float(rng.uniform(0, 360)) per crop, stack, permute to NCHW, float()/255.0 - exactly the baseline's tensor construction, just re-run per epoch. Draw angles from the same rng so --seed still yields a deterministic run. Batching within the epoch (torch.randperm, slices of 64, .to(device)) is unchanged.
10. Update loss call for the new contract: `loss = loss_fn(model.forward_logits(xb), yb)`.
11. Wall-time guard: per-epoch extraction of 6000 crops (182px window slice + PIL rotate + 128px center crop) should cost roughly 3-8 s/epoch; total run target 15-25 min on MPS. If measured extraction exceeds ~15 s/epoch, fall back to pre-generating a pool of 8 rotated uint8 variants per crop at load time and sampling one per crop per epoch from the pool (rng.integers) - same rng, same tensor construction. Do not silently drop the fresh-rotation mechanism.
Everything else - imports style, model.cpu() before export, ONNX export path <out-dir>/models/<area>.onnx, train_info.json read-append-write, the printed json summary - stays untouched.
